# Weft

Weft is a free, open-source Rust compiler for compact website descriptions. Source files use `.wft`. The compiler will emit native HTML, raw CSS, and optional isolated browser JavaScript.

## Source contract

- Static HTML is the default output.
- JavaScript exists only for explicit `island` declarations.
- Styling declarations express semantic layout and design tokens; output is ordinary CSS, not Tailwind/UnoCSS classes or CSS-in-JS.
- Links compile to `<a>` elements. Future mutations should prefer HTML forms and server responses.
- All user-visible text must be HTML-escaped.
- Every text-rendering field accepts a `TextExpr`: literals, identifiers, and `identifier * integer` joined with `+`. State-dependent expressions are valid only inside their declaring counter island.
- Invalid syntax must stop compilation and include a source location.

## Supported core grammar

```wft
site Name
theme: brand violet; ink slate; radius lg

page /:
  hero:
    eyebrow "Text"
    title "Text"
    text "Text"
    actions:
      "Label" -> /path primary

  section name cards 3:
    card "Title" "Description"

  island counter:
    label "Seats"
    state seats=5
    range seats 1..100
    text "$" + seats * 12 + "/month"
```

The grammar above is the shipped initial subset. `page /:` is currently the only supported page route; only the `counter` island is supported. Read `docs/language.md` for the exact contract.

## Commands

```sh
cargo fmt --check
cargo test
cargo clippy -- -D warnings
```
